column1: Cacio e Pepe,What are the directions of Cacio e Pepe?,directions,5,"Reference 1: The directions of Cacio e Pepe are: Cook the pasta al dente, drain.
column2: Put the put back on the stove.
column3: Immediately sprinkle the finely grated cheese over the pasta, and mix in some of the water used to boil the pasta, until the cheese melts into a light, almost watery, creamy sauce.

column3: While the pasta cooks, melt butter in a large saute pan over medium heat.
column4: Add the fresh cracked pepper.
column5: When the butter begins to bubble, turn off the flame and remove from heat.
column6: When the pasta is ready, add the noodles and 2 1/2 tablespoons of the water to the saute pan.
column7: Cook over medium high heat until the liquid bubbles and thickens, tossing the pasta as needed.

column2: Add the spaghetti and cook until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes.

column6: Toss well to coat, adding the pasta water as needed to make a thick, creamy sauce that coats the pasta strands.
column7: Season with salt and lots of freshly ground black pepper.
column8: Divide the pasta among four plates, serve immediately..

column1: Curry Chicken Salad,What are the directions of Curry Chicken Salad?,directions,9,"Reference 1: The directions of Curry Chicken Salad are: Toss together chicken, rice and celery in large bowl.
column2: Blend remaining ingredients.
column3: Stir into chicken mixture.
column4: Serve on shredded lettuce and garnish with black olives.
column5: Yields 6 servings..

column1: Reference 2: The directions of Curry Chicken Salad are: Mix all ingredients except Miracle Whip and nuts and refrigerate for 3 hours.
column2: Fold in Miracle Whip and nuts before serving.
column3: Serves 12..

column1: Reference 3: The directions of Curry Chicken Salad are: Hard boil eggs, then chop. (I put eggs in a pan in cold water, bring to boil, remove from heat, cover, let stand 17 minutes, drain water, cover with cold water and ice for 5 minutes, then peel).
column2: While eggs are cooking, dice chicken, celery, pickle and onion (finely for hors d'oeuvres, coarsely for sandwiches or salads).
column3: Mix chicken, celery, onion, pickle, and eggs in medium sized bowl.
column4: Add mayonnaise, and mix together adding sugar, salt, and pepper to your taste.
column5: Serve on bed of lettuce for salad, on toast for sandwiches, or stuff puffs for hors d'oeuvres. Part of prep time is during cooking of the eggs..

column1: Reference 4: The directions of Curry Chicken Salad are: Quarter, core and coarsely chop the apple. (Don't peel it.) Toss it with the lime juice.
column2: Add the mayonnaise, yogurt, mustard, salt, curry powder and grated fresh ginger, if using. Stir well to combine.
column3: Add the chicken, the celery and the chopped herbs. Toss lightly.
column4: Test for salt and add more, if necessary. Add pepper to taste and toss again.
column5: Before eating, add the nuts and toss one more time. If taking this for lunch later, put the nuts on top, then mix them in before eating, if you want them to remain as crisp as possible. (They'll get a bit soggy if they sit in the dressing for more than hour or two.)
column6: Enjoy!! ,o)
column7: N.B. I've indicated that the fresh ginger is optional because it actually adds a bit of heat, which some people like, but others really don't. Add it or not, to taste.
column8: About the mustard: I like to use my own Apple Mustard, or pear Mostarda Mantovana (which I make often during pear season!) in this salad.
column9: Toast the cumin, coriander and cardamom lightly in a small skillet just until fragrant, shaking the pan frequently. The minute they seem to be turning a darker color, remove all of the seeds right away, lest they burn.
column10: Break the cinnamon stick into about five or six pieces. Very lightly toast it in the skillet, for no more than a minute or so on medium heat.
column11: Grind the toasted seeds, the cinnamon stick, the mustard seeds and the cloves to a fine powder. (Check the grinder once or twice to dislodge any cinnamon pieces that may have stuck to the blade.)
column12: Put into a jar and add the turmeric and the cayenne, if using. Put on the lid and shake well to combine. Use within a few weeks..

column2: Add chicken, celery, and raisins, toss well.
column3: Combine mayonnaise and next 5 ingredients in a small bowl, pour over chicken mixture, and toss well.
column4: Sprinkle with chopped almonds.
column5: Cover and chill at least 1 hour. Note: If you don't have 3 cups of leftover chicken, cook 1 pound of skinned, boned chicken breast halves on a baking sheet in the oven at 450° for 12 to 14 minutes or until the juices run clear.
column6: Toast the almonds on the same baking sheet during the last 3 minutes of cooking..

column2: Chill for 30 minutes.

column1: Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes,What are the directions of Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes?,directions,9,"Reference 1: The directions of Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes are: Heat oven to 450 degrees.
column2: Place garlic and shallots in a 8-inch square baking pan, drizzle with oil.
column3: Cover with foil and roast 40 minutes, turning shallots occasionally, or until they are tender and golden.
column4: Cool.
column5: Squeeze garlic cloves from skins, place in food processor with roasted shallots and any remaining oil in pan. Process until smooth.
column6: Can be made ahead, cover and refrigerate 24 hours..

column1: Reference 2: The directions of Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes are: Preheat oven to 450 degrees.
column2: Place garlic in pan and brush with olive oil and salt and pepper.
column3: Roast for 35 minute until golden brown.
column4: Let cool, then squeeze garlic from head.
column5: Boil potatoes for about 15 to 20 minute.
column6: Drain.
column7: Add garlic and butter and mash.
column8: Add milk until desired texture..

column1: Reference 3: The directions of Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes are: Preheat oven to 425°.
column2: Remove papery outer skin from garlic bulb, but do not peel or separate the cloves.
column3: Cut off top of garlic bulb, exposing individual cloves, brush with oil.
column4: Wrap in heavy-duty foil.
column5: Bake until cloves are softened, 30-35 minutes.
column6: Unwrap and cool 10 minutes.
column7: Meanwhile, place potatoes in a large saucepan, cover with water.
column8: Bring to a boil.
column9: Reduce heat, cook, uncovered, until potatoes are tender, 10-15 minutes.
column10: Squeeze garlic cloves into a bowl, mash with a fork until smooth.
column11: Drain potatoes, return to pan.
column12: Add garlic, mash potatoes to desired consistency, gradually adding remaining ingredients..

column1: Reference 4: The directions of Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes are: Preheat oven to 375 F. Wash and chop the potatoes into one-inch cubes, leave the skin on.
column2: Into a roasting pan add the chopped potatoes, garlic cloves, rosemary, thyme, and olive oil. Season with the salt and pepper. Mix well.
column3: Roast at 375 F for 50 minutes to one hour.
column4: Once cooked, take the pan out of the oven and cover with tin foil. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
column5: After the potatoes have rested remove the larger sprigs of rosemary and thyme and discard them.
column6: Add the sour cream, milk, and green onions and mash everything all together. You want the texture to be chunky and rustic, not smooth.
column7: Taste and adjust seasoning.
column8: Notes:
column9: 1. If the potatoes are too dry add a little bit more sour cream.
column10: 2. You can use whatever milk you have on hand in place of skim. I myself tend to use 1% lately. I read recently that your body absorbs the nutrients in milk better if there is some fat.
column11: 3. This is a rustic dish so it is okay if there are big sprigs of the herbs mixed in the potatoes. Just remove the larger pieces and the stems. An alternative to this is to remove the leaves from the stems and finely chop them before you add them to the roasting pan..

column1: Reference 5: The directions of Roasted Garlic Mashed Potatoes are: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, and add 1 tablespoon salt.
column2: Bring to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat so the water simmers gently.
column3: Cook until there is no resistance when a fork is inserted into the potatoes, about 20 minutes.
column4: Warm the milk in a small pot over low heat.
column5: Drain the potatoes and, while theyre hot, pass them through a food mill or potato ricer into a large mixing bowl.
column6: (If you do not have a ricer or food mill you can use a potato masher, but the potatoes wont be as fluffy.)
column7: Add the milk, butter, and garlic puree, stirring with a wooden spoon to blend into the potatoes, season with 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper.
column8: Feel free to add more milk to achieve the consistency that you like.
column9: Cover and keep the potatoes warm until ready to serve..

column2: Drain into colander.
column3: Rice or mash potatoes and place back in pot.
column4: Warm milk, butter add cream cheese in a pot over low heat to a simmer.
column5: Stir into the potatoes adding the remaining ingredients folding in well.
column6: Place in serving bowl and garnish with additional kosher salt and paprika..

column14: Add shrimp to skillet and saute about 2 minute until shrimp lightly browned.

column1: Whole Wheat Bread,What are the directions of Whole Wheat Bread?,directions,9,"Reference 1: The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: Put oatmeal into boiling water and let stand.
column2: Dissolve yeast in warm water.
column3: Add oil, add oatmeal mixture and all other ingredients.
column4: Mix well as you go along.
column5: Add bread flour until you get a stiff workable dough.
column6: Knead well.
column7: Let rise.
column8: Knead again and shape into loaves.
column9: Let rise and bake at 350° until done (approximately 20 to 25 minutes)..

column1: Reference 2: The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: In a mixing bowl, combine eggs, yogurt and milk.
column2: Beat thoroughly with a wooden spoon. Add the honey and oil.
column3: Add the dry ingredients and blend thoroughly.
column4: Pour into greased muffin tins.
column5: Bake at 425° for 15 minutes.
column6: Makes 12 large muffins..

column1: Reference 3: The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: In bowl mix both flours together.
column2: In another large bowl, mix all other ingredients together.
column3: Add to flour mixture.
column4: Knead well.
column5: Put in greased bowl.
column6: Cover and let rise until double. Work down good, put in greased loaf pans.
column7: Let rise.
column8: Bake at 350° for 30 minutes..

column1: Reference 4: The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: Preheat oven to 375°.
column2: Combine wheat and white flours.
column3: In 1/2 cup lukewarm water, add a pinch of brown sugar and flour and packages of yeast.
column4: Let mixture rise until 4 times in volume.
column5: Add all remaining ingredients, mix.
column6: Fold in yeast.
column7: Add rest of liquid, knead for 10 minutes.
column8: Put in greased bowl, cover and place in warm oven until bread has doubled in size.
column9: Punch down, divide and place in 2 greased pans.
column10: Let rise again until doubled. Bake for 45 minutes.
column11: Remove from pans to cool..

column1: Reference 5: The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: Place yeast in 1/2 cup warm water with 1 teaspoon sugar and set aside.
column2: In large mixing bowl, put warm liquid molasses, salt and oil, then add yeast and stir.
column3: Sift in about half or 2/3 of flour and stir.
column4: Continue adding flour until the dough is stiff enough to work by hand on floured counter top.
column5: Knead until smooth, cover and let set about 15 minutes.
column6: Knead again, place in greased bowl, cover and let rise until double in bulk.
column7: Knead and shape into loaves.
column8: Place in loaf pans, cover and let rise about 1 hour.
column9: Bake at 325° to 350° for 40 minutes to 1 hour depending on size of loaves.
column10: Less time for smaller loaves..

column1: Reference 6: The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: Dissolve yeast and 1 teaspoon sugar in 1/3 cup warm water, stir well, and let stand 5 minutes.
column2: Combine remaining sugar and warm water, shortening, and salt in a large mixing bowl, stir until shortening melts.
column3: Stir in yeast mixture, cereal, and enough flour to make a soft dough.
column4: Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface, and knead 10 minutes or until smooth and elastic.
column5: Place dough in a greased bowl, turning to grease top.
column6: Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in bulk.
column7: Punch dough down, cover and repeat rising procedure 1 hour or until doubled in bulk.
column8: Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface.
column9: Divide dough in half, cover and let rest 10 minutes.
column10: Shape into loaves and place in 2 greased 7 1/2- x 3- x 2- inch loaf pans.
column11: Cover and repeat rising procedure 1 hour or until doubled in bulk.
column12: Bake at 350° for 55 minutes or until loaves sound hollow when tapped.
column13: Remove bread from pans, and bake an additional 3 minutes to crisp bottoms of loaves.
column14: Cool on wire racks..

column1: Reference 7: The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: Add the warm water to a warmed bowl (run it under some hot water so it will keep the temperature).
column2: Add the sugar.
column3: Stir briefly to dissolve.
column4: Sprinkle the half packet of yeast over the top. DO NOT STIR.
column5: Cover the bowl with a towel and let rest for a few minutes.
column6: Check yeast to see if it's puffing up. If the yeast is still grainy and not puffy, throw it out and start all over. Inactive yeast will cause your bread to flop.
column7: Add the whole wheat flour and stir vigorously with a whisk for a minute.
column8: Add the salt and the canola oil.
column9: Stir vigorously again.
column10: Add 1 cup of flour bread and stir with a wooden spoon.
column11: Continue to add the bread flour 1/2 cup at a time until it is too stiff to stir and is hardly sticky at all.
column12: Dump dough onto a floured surface and knead with your hands.
column13: Add a light sprinklings of flour as needed and continue to knead until the dough is nice and tight.
column14: Place the dough into a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a towel and let it rise until doubled in size (at least 30-40 minutes).
column15: Punch down the dough to release the air bubbles, cover again and let it rise again.
column16: Roll the dough out on a lightly floured surface and form a loaf.
column17: Place into a greased loaf pan and allow to rise for about 20 minutes.
column18: Now preheat your oven to 375 degrees F.
column19: If you want a nice sheen to the top of your loaf, this is the time to brush on some egg wash.
column20: Scramble the 1 egg in a bowl with about a 1/4 cup of water and brush this mixture over the top of your loaf.
column21: Bake loaf for 35-45 minutes.
column22: Check for doneness by pulling the loaf out and tapping it on the bottom. If it sounds hollow, it's done. If it still sounds dense, put it back in for a few more minutes and check again.
column23: When it's done, immediately remove it from the pan and place on a cooling rack to to rest.
column24: Cut it and eat it! Just remember not to wrap the bread while it's still warm because it will get soggy.
column25: Let it come to room temperature before storing it in a Ziploc bag. It stores well in the fridge and the freezer..

column1: Reference 8: The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: In your mixing bowl add the warm water (110-120 degrees), yeast and two cups of the flour.
column2: Stir well and let it sponge for 30 minutes.
column3: Stir to blend and add one cup flour and turn your mixer on low.
column4: Add flour by 1/2 cupfuls until the dough cleans the side of the bowl and is no longer sticky.
column5: Let it knead in mixer for about 6-8 minutes.
column6: After is has finished kneading let it rise in the mixer until it is doubled.
column7: After it has doubled, put a light coat of oil on hands and take dough to an oiled cutting board and cut into two pieces.
column8: Form these pieces into loaf shape and put into loaf pan.
column9: Keep loaves covered with a lightweight drying cloth while the bread rises.
column10: It should rise to about 1 1/2 inches above the rim of the pans.
column11: Put loaves in oven and turn on heat to 350 degrees.
column12: Let bake in oven for 25-30 minutes.
column13: Remove from the oven.
column14: Remove from pan and cover with a clean towel which helps soften crusts.
column15: You can store in a plastic bread bag but don't put in bread bag too soon or the bag will sweat..

column43: Let rise again until doubled. Bake for 45 minutes.
column44: Remove from pans to cool.."", ""The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: Place yeast in 1/2 cup warm water with 1 teaspoon sugar and set aside.

column56: Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface, and knead 10 minutes or until smooth and elastic.

column58: Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in bulk.
column59: Punch dough down, cover and repeat rising procedure 1 hour or until doubled in bulk.

column61: Divide dough in half, cover and let rest 10 minutes.
column62: Shape into loaves and place in 2 greased 7 1/2- x 3- x 2- inch loaf pans.

column66: Cool on wire racks.."", ""The directions of Whole Wheat Bread are: Add the warm water to a warmed bowl (run it under some hot water so it will keep the temperature).

column1: Chicken Curry,What are the directions of Chicken Curry?,directions,10,"Reference 1: The directions of Chicken Curry are: Heat oven to 350 degrees.
column2: Coat a 12x7x2"" baking pan with nonstick cooking spray.
column3: Spoon cooked rice into baking dish and spread evenly.
column4: Scatter 3/4 of the broccoli over the rice.
column5: Chop the chicken into bite size pieces and spread evenly over top.
column6: In a large bowl, whisk the soup, mayo, milk, lemon juice and curry powder until blended and smooth.
column7: Pour evenly over the top.
column8: Sprinkle remaining broccoli over the top.
column9: Bake 350 degree oven covered for 30 min.
column10: Uncover and bake 15 more minutes.
column11: Serve hot..

column1: Reference 2: The directions of Chicken Curry are: In a large, deep skillet, cook the onion in the oil over medium heat, stirring, until golden brown, about 10 minutes.
column2: Add the curry powder and cook, stirring, for 30 seconds.
column3: Stir in the tomato juice, wine, and chutney and simmer for 2 minutes to blend the flavors.
column4: Add the chicken and simmer, covered, stirring occasionally, until cooked through, about 10 minutes.
column5: Add the salt.
column6: Serve half the chicken curry over rice.
column7: Top with the peanuts, bell pepper, and scallions.
column8: Freeze the remaining chicken curry..

column1: Reference 3: The directions of Chicken Curry are: Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
column2: Add onion and garlic, cook 4 minutes or until onion is tender.
column3: Add the chicken, cook 4 minutes.
column4: Add curry powder and marjoram, cook 1 minute.
column5: Add tomato, broth, and pepper, reduce heat, and simmer 15 minutes.
column6: Remove from heat.
column7: Combine yogurt and flour, stir with a whisk, and add to chicken mixture.
column8: Cook 1 minute or until slightly thick.
column9: Serve mixture over couscous, top with raisins, if desired..

column1: Reference 4: The directions of Chicken Curry are: Pat chicken dry and sprinkle with 1/2 teaspoon salt.
column2: Heat oil in a 12-inch heavy skillet over moderately high heat until hot but not smoking
column3: Brown chicken, turning over once, about 5 minutes total.
column4: Transfer chicken with tongs to a plate.
column5: Stir garlic, curry, and cayenne into fat in skillet, then add coconut milk, tomatoes with their juice, currants, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and bring to a simmer.
column6: Add okra and chicken along with any juices accumulated on plate and briskly simmer, partially covered, until chicken is cooked through, 15 to 20 minutes.
column7: Sprinkle with cashews..

column1: Reference 5: The directions of Chicken Curry are: Wash and Cut chicken in bite-sized pieces
column2: Marinade chicken in cooking bowl
column3: Add in: 0.76 g pepper, 3.01 g salt, 8.87 g sugar, 13.61 g oil, 6.0 g curry powder, 0.79 g garlic powder, 1.1 g onion powder.
column4: Mix and Marinade for half an hour.
column5: Wash and cut carrots and potatoes in bite-sized pieces
column6: soak potatoes in water bowl to prevent browning
column7: dice the onion
column8: warm up medium-size pot
column9: add 13.61 g oil, diced onion, 13.47 g butter (low heat)
column10: let simmer for 5 minutes with lid closed
column11: add marinaded chicken, mix and close lid - mix occasionally, for about 10 minutes until chicken is fully cooked
column12: add in chicken broth and coconut milk
column13: stir occasionally and cover lid, wait for broth to simmer - cook for approx. 8 to 10 minutes on low heat
column14: taste and season with a little salt/sugar/curry powder (if needed, depending on individual taste)
column15: add in carrots and potatoes
column16: mix well and close lid, wait for simmering - about 10 minutes for carrots and potatoes to cook.

column1: Reference 6: The directions of Chicken Curry are: In a large pan, heat oil on medium heat for one minute.
column2: Add onions and cinnamon, and saute for five to eight minutes, until onions are golden.
column3: Add garlic and saute for four more minutes. Add ginger, tomatoes, salt, pepper, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala and cayenne.
column4: Cook the masala for five minutes, until the oil separates.
column5: Add chicken to the masala and stir thoroughly.
column6: Cook for 10 minutes, until the chicken looks cooked on the outside.
column7: Add sour cream, cream or coconut milk, and stir.
column8: Increase the heat to medium-high.
column9: When curry starts to boil, reduce the heat to medium, cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring two or three times, until chicken is completely cooked.
column10: Note: poke the thighs with a knife. If the meat is still pink, cook for five more minutes.
column11: Remove and discard the cinnamon sticks and add chickpeas.
column12: If using bone-in chicken, cool curry for at least half an hour and transfer cooked chicken to a mixing bowl.
column13: After chicken has cooled a bit, peel meat off the bones and discard the bones.
column14: Stir the chicken back into the curry and heat medium heat until it starts to boil lightly.
column15: Stir in cilantro immediately before serving..

column1: Reference 7: The directions of Chicken Curry are: In a large plastic bag combine flour, curry powder, cumin, and salt.
column2: Add chicken, a few pieces at a time, seal and shake to coat.
column3: In a 3-1/2- or 4-quart slow cooker combine potatoes, carrots, apple, onion, garlic, jalapeno peppers, and chicken bouillon.
column4: Top with chicken.
column5: Pour water over chicken mixture.
column6: Cover, cook on low-heat setting for 6 to 8 hours or on high-heat setting for 3 to 4 hours.
column7: If using low-heat setting, turn the slow cooker to high-heat setting.
column8: Stir coconut milk into chicken mixture.
column9: Cover, cook for 30 minutes more. Serve over hot cooked rice.
column10: Sprinkle each serving with raisins and peanuts..

column1: Reference 8: The directions of Chicken Curry are: Rub the chicken pieces with the curry paste.
column2: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
column3: Stir fry the chicken and add a few spoonfuls of broth to the pan when the chicken is almost done so that it stays moist.
column4: When cooked, remove the chicken and pan juices to a bowl (scrape to keep as much chili paste as possible) and set aside for later.

column12: Serve curry on rice, and with yogurt on the side if you need something to tame the spice..

column1: Reference 9: The directions of Chicken Curry are: Combine the chicken with the Madras curry powder, paprika, and 1/2 tsp salt.

column1: Pistachio Cake,What are the directions of Pistachio Cake?,directions,10,"Reference 1: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Mix cake mix, pudding mix, oil, water and eggs together.
column2: Fold in nuts and coconut.
column3: Put in greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes..

column1: Reference 2: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Mix 3 minutes on medium speed.
column2: Bake at 350° in Bundt pan for 35 to 45 minutes or until slightly brown..

column1: Reference 3: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Combine all ingredients well.
column2: Pour into well-greased tube pan.
column3: Bake at 350° for 50 to 55 minutes..

column1: Reference 4: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Place all ingredients in one bowl.
column2: Mix at low speed for 1 minute and at high speed for 3 minutes.
column3: Pour into Bundt or tube pan.
column4: Cook at 350° for 45 to 50 minutes.
column5: Sprinkle confectioners sugar when cool..

column1: Reference 5: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: In a large bowl, mix cake mix, eggs, water, pudding mix, orange juice and oil.
column2: Grease and flour a Bundt pan.
column3: Place 2/3 of batter in pan.
column4: With remaining batter, mix the chocolate syrup and pour on top.
column5: Do not stir.
column6: Bake in preheated oven at 350° for 50 minutes or until done..

column1: Reference 6: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Beat together yellow cake mix, instant pudding, eggs, oil and sour cream, beat well.
column2: Mix sugar, nuts and cinnamon separately. Put half of first mixture in a greased tube pan, then half of sugar mixture.
column3: Add remaining yellow cake mixture and sugar mixture.
column4: Bake at 350° about 35 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean..

column1: Reference 7: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Combine all ingredients, including 1 package pudding, in large bowl and mix well with electric mixer for 2 or 3 minutes.
column2: Pour into tube pan.
column3: Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
column4: Cool completely, then frost with the following:.

column1: Reference 8: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Mix cake mix, 1 package instant pudding, eggs, club soda, oil and nuts as you would to make cake.
column2: Bake at 350° for 30 to 35 minutes.
column3: Let cool.
column4: Mix milk, Dream Whip and 1 pudding mix and frost..

column1: Reference 9: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Preheat oven to 350F.
column2: Butter a 13- by 9-inch metal cake pan, then line bottom with wax paper.
column3: Butter paper and dust pan with some flour, knocking out excess.
column4: Pulse pistachios in a food processor until finely ground (be careful not to overprocess into a paste).
column5: Add 1 cup flour, baking powder, cardamom, and salt and pulse once or twice to mix.
column6: Combine milk and vanilla in a measuring cup.
column7: Beat together butter and sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer until pale and fluffy.
column8: Add eggs 1 at a time, beating well after each addition.
column9: Alternately add pistachio flour and milk in batches, beginning and ending with flour, and mix at low speed until just combined.
column10: Spread batter evenly in cake pan and bake in middle of oven until a tester comes out clean, about 20 minutes.
column11: Cool in pan on a rack 10 minutes, then run a thin knife around sides of cake and invert onto rack.
column12: Remove paper and reinvert cake onto a platter.
column13: Cut into squares and serve warm or at room temperature..

column1: Reference 10: The directions of Pistachio Cake are: Heat the oven to 300 degrees.
column2: Grease a 12 x 4 1/2 x 2 3/4-inch loaf pan with 4 tsp of the butter and line with baking parchment.
column3: Soften the remaining butter.
column4: Finely grate the lemon peel.
column5: Split the vanilla bean and scrape out the seeds.
column6: Finely grind the almonds and pistachios together (it's easier if you can find these ready ground!
column7: I thought my arm was going to fall off).
column8: Beat the butter and the sugar until light and fluffy.
column9: Beat in the eggs, one at a time.
column10: Add the lemon peel and vanilla seeds, then fold in the nuts and sift in the flour.
column11: Spoon the batter into the pan and bake for 45-60 minutes.
column12: The cake is ready when a skewer comes out clean.
column13: Leave to cool in the pan, then turn out.
column14: For the topping, grate the lemon peel and squeeze the juice.
column15: Halve the pistachios.
column16: Mix the lemon juice with the sugar, boil until reduced to a syrup, then add the peel.
